subject: Request: CloudVitals volume incentive carveout — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CloudVitals volume incentive carveout — exec approval needed

Team —

Quick summary: CloudVitals (prospect -> rapid pilot) pushed back on standard onboarding credits and committed-rate tiers. They expect a heavy initial burst of embed + chat traffic (estimated 1.2B tokens in the first 90 days) because they plan to re-ingest historical telemetry for model tuning. They’re asking for a steep onboarding/rebate package that sits outside our pricing guardrails: 30% onboarding credit + 25% per-token rebate for first 6 months.

Why this matters: if we don’t accommodate some concession they will roll to a competitor. But the ask materially impacts unit economics given dedicated GPU / VPC requirements. Their business case: long-term ARR potential > $1.8M ARR after year 1 if we secure a 12‑month commit.

Recommended carveout (commercial ops + risk balanced):
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% of first 3 months' committed spend (not 30%)
- Usage rebate: 12% per-token rebate for the first 90 days only
- Minimum commitment: 6 months billed commitment with a 12-month preferred term
- Routing & cost controls: require prefix caching + routing fallback to quantized model for non-sensitive workloads
- Contractual protections: SLA amendment (see attached) that limits exposure and requires consumption reporting monthly

Attachments: CloudVitals_Pricing_Summary_Q4.xlsx (breaks down modeling) and Draft_SLA_Amendment_CloudVitals.pdf

As this falls outside our published discount matrix, I need VP/CFO clearance to move forward. Marcus/Markus — can you review and confirm whether the proposed carveout is approvable as-is or whether we should tighten conditions (e.g., shorter rebate window, higher commit floor)? Requested timeline: need an answer by EOD Tuesday so we can respond to Tara before they finalize vendor shortlist on Oct 8.

Thanks —
Naomi
Senior Manager, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(attachment: CloudVitals_Pricing_Summary_Q4.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CloudVitals volume incentive carveout — exec approval needed

Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up. A few reactions from pricing/finance POV: 

1) Margin impact: 12% rebate on a 1.2B token burst is substantial; modeled delta to gross margin = ~9.1% in Q1 with dedicated capacity uplift.
2) Precedent risk: CloudVitals is asking for a 6-months+ heavy-burst carveout; if we accept long tails without strict gates we risk similar asks from other health-analytics accounts.

Alternate structure to reduce cash exposure while keeping the deal alive: 
- Move from a percentage rebate to token credits for onboarding: give a fixed token credit pool equivalent to ~10% of modeled Q1 spend that can only be used in the first 90 days. That caps downside and is easier to recognize.
- Combine with an accelerated commit ramp: if they hit 80% of expected usage for 2 consecutive months we trigger an incremental 5% rebate for months 4–6.

Operational asks: must require data retention & deletion clauses for the re-ingested telemetry and a cap on production model size that needs dedicated GPUs. Otherwise compute cost will run away.

If Marcus/Markus are comfortable with the capped-credit approach I can update the financials and show the adjusted margin impact (likely <3% SNR hit).

—Karthik
Head of Commercial Finance
(attachment: none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 14:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CloudVitals volume incentive carveout — exec approval needed

Looping Jordan for commercial posture and Marcus for VP-level sign-off. Jordan — please validate that the deal motion (pilot -> committed year) and technical gating align with CS/solutions.

I like Karthik’s capped-credit option — it reduces financial tail risk and preserves our ability to upsell. My ask for executive sign-off would be conditional on: 
- token-credit cap (no percent rebates)
- explicit 90-day rebate/credit window
- minimum 6-month commitment with true-up invoicing at month 3
- SLA amendment with consumption reporting and rollback trigger if usage exceeds modeled envelope by >40%

Marcus — recommend we approve conditionally and instruct Legal to fold the SLA amendment into the pilot MSA. Please advise if Markus needs to sign off as CFO.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy
(attachment: Draft_SLA_Amendment_CloudVitals.pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CloudVitals volume incentive carveout — exec approval needed

Thanks team — reviewed the numbers and risks. I approve a conditional carveout on the following terms (finance/CFO sign-off):

1) Token credit pool in lieu of a percent rebate: credit value capped at $150k equivalent to estimated Q1 excess consumption (applies only to first 90 days).
2) Minimum financial commitment: 6 months minimum billing commitment; preferred 12-month term documented in the SOW.
3) True-up & reporting: monthly consumption reporting; if actuals exceed modeled envelope by >40% we reserve the right to pause credits and require remediation (route to quantized model / cost share).
4) Legal to add SLA amendment with explicit compute-cap and deletion clause for re-ingested telemetry.
5) Approval is contingent on a scaled-back onboarding credit of 10% (applied to first invoice only).

If Commercial wants to proceed, Legal/CS should share the revised MSA/SOW with CloudVitals and I’ll sign off on the financials once the exact credit language is inserted. This preserves runway for the account and limits our cash exposure.

Approved — Markus Klein
VP Finance (acting CFO)
Redwood Inference
(markus.klein@redwood.com)
